problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14058907/assets/00547d8271d0c277de2bd1992d759e0157a80c9caf05cfb1020550853ae7b8b3.png)

Evaluate the line integral ${\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=(x+y)\,i+(1-x)\,j$ and $C$ is the arc of the ellipse $9{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}=36$  traversed from the point $A(0,3)$ to the point $B(-2,0).$
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Notice that we can write its equation as

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}=1.
$$

So, our curve is a part-ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal and vertical semiaxes $2$ and $3$ respectively. This curve can be parameterized as

$$
r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le t\le \pi .
$$

So, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(x+y)\,i+(1-x)\,j \\  & =(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =((2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j)\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+(1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot 3\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-6({sin}^{2}⁡t-{cos}^{2}⁡t) \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t+3\operatorname{cos}⁡t-6)\,dt \\  & =[\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+3\operatorname{sin}⁡t-6t]_{\pi /2}^{\pi } \\  & =[1+0-6\pi ]-[-1+3-3\pi ] \\  & =-1-3\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

Evaluate the line integral ∫CF(r)⋅dr, where F(x,y)=(x+y)i+(1−x)j and C is the arc of the ellipse 9x2+4y2=36 traversed from the point A(0,3) to the point B(−2,0).

a
3π
b
−2+3π
c
4−3π
d
−1−3π
e
−9π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the formula ∫CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Notice that we can write its equation as

x24+y29=1.

So, our curve is a part-ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal and vertical semiaxes 2 and 3 respectively. This curve can be parameterized as

r(t)=2cos⁡ti+3sin⁡tj,π2≤t≤π.

So, along the curve C, we have x=2cos⁡t,y=3sin⁡t.

As a result,

F(r(t))=(x+y)i+(1−x)j=(2cos⁡t+3sin⁡t)i+(1−2cos⁡t)j.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(2cos⁡t)i+ddt(3sin⁡t)j=−2sin⁡ti+3cos⁡tj.

Therefore, F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=((2cos⁡t+3sin⁡t)i+(1−2cos⁡t)j)⋅(−2sin⁡ti+3cos⁡tj)=(2cos⁡t+3sin⁡t)⋅(−2sin⁡t)+(1−2cos⁡t)⋅3cos⁡t=−4sin⁡tcos⁡t+3cos⁡t−6(sin2⁡t−cos2⁡t)=−2sin⁡2t+3cos⁡t−6.

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

∫CF(r)⋅dr=∫π/2πF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫π/2π(−2sin⁡2t+3cos⁡t−6)dt=[cos⁡2t+3sin⁡t−6t]π/2π=[1+0−6π]−[−1+3−3π]=−1−3π
